subject: Sizing advisory: phased reserved commit and GPU price-sensitivity playbook
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@heliolabs.ai>
Cc: procurement@heliolabs.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing advisory: phased reserved commit and GPU price-sensitivity playbook

Team / Sarah,

Following our QBR and the sizing run we ran last week, I put together a short advisory that ties the Helio Labs Reserved Capacity ask to a phased commit cadence and explicit GPU-price sensitivity triggers. Attached: HL-sizing-model.xlsx (workbook with monthly token forecasts + GPU SKU mix) and commit-term-draft.pdf (draft term language).

High level / why this matters:
- Helio's projected peak throughput pushes them into a 2–3 GPU-pool configuration for production inference; committing fixed capacity without phase gates materially increases Redwood's exposure to GPU spot/market volatility.
- We can protect Helio's unit economics and Redwood's margin by offering a two-option structure with explicit indexation and contingency triggers rather than a single flat deep discount.

Proposal (short):
Option A — Phased 18-month commit (recommended)
- Year 1: 12-month firm commitment at 75% of forecasted baseline (monthly true-up)
- Year 2: 6-month exercised option to scale to 100% based on rolling forecast
- Discount: 15% on baseline unit pricing; quarterly GPU-indexation clause with a +/-10% band (customer protected to floor).

Option B — Longer 24-month commit (higher discount)
- 24-month firm commit at 90% baseline
- Discount: 22% upfront, but subject to a price-sensitivity trigger: if average GPU cost index increases >18% vs benchmark, Redwood can request renegotiation or limited credit offsets.

What I need from internal team:
1) Finance: quick sanity check on the 22% break-even on Option B and what threshold we need to escalate for exec sign-off.
2) Legal: review indexation language (I added two short clauses in the attached PDF).
3) Sales/AE: confirm Helio's tolerance for an 18-month phased approach vs wanting a single commitment.

Sarah — if you can confirm whether Helio has a firm procurement window in December (procurement mentioned year-end approvals), we can time the final proposal to that cadence.

Thanks,

Olga Petrov
Principal, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: HL-sizing-model.xlsx (spreadsheet), commit-term-draft.pdf (term language)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Sarah Park <sarah@heliolabs.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing advisory: phased reserved commit and GPU price-sensitivity playbook

Olga —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple quick notes from Finance POV:
- Option B with a 22% nominal discount looks okay on a gross margin calc only if we have either (a) a contractual price-floor for pass-through GPU costs or (b) an explicit escalation path for >18% GPU cost inflation.
- Anything that forces us into an indefinite renegotiation (open-ended) will need exec approval — threshold for that is discounts >20% or potential margin erosion >8% over NPV.

Can you add a simple sensitivity table in the HL-sizing-model.xlsx showing P50/P90 GPU cost scenarios (we should show “worst-case + 25% GPU cost impact” and the resulting margin delta). I can run a quick NPV if you need.

—Marcus
Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Park <sarah@heliolabs.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliolabs.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing advisory: phased reserved commit and GPU price-sensitivity playbook

Olga / Marcus,

Thanks — this framing is helpful. A few notes from Helio Procurement: we have a December 15 procurement committee deadline for any vendor contract to be included in our FY27 capex/opex plan. Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood include an explicit "price protection floor" for the first 12 months of the contract? Procurement is comfortable with an indexation clause, but they want a one-year floor to avoid immediate re-pricing risk.
- Helio prefers an 18-month option over 24 if it keeps the downside managed; they may accept the 22% structure if there is a hard floor or an escrow mechanism for overages.
- Please attach a short redlines-friendly version for our legal team — we review word-for-word.

I've attached our procurement questions PDF for reference (Helio-procurement-questions.pdf). Happy to jump on a short call Friday to close open points.

Best,
Sarah Park
Head of Cloud Ops, Helio Labs
sarah@heliolabs.ai
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah@heliolabs.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing advisory: phased reserved commit and GPU price-sensitivity playbook

Sarah —

Appreciate the clarity. I updated the draft to reflect a 12-month hard price-protection floor and made the indexation more prescriptive (quarterly measurement against our GPU cost index, with a 6% bilateral negotiation corridor before either side can trigger the renegotiation flow). New language also includes an escrow credit mechanic (if GPU indexation causes redwood >10% margin compression, Helio receives a capped credit; conversely, if costs fall, we pass through gains at a 50/50 split). See commit-term-draft.pdf (page 2).

To summarize two final customer-facing options (revised):
Option A (Recommended) — Phased 18-month
- 12-month price floor + quarterly index check (+/- 6% corridor).
- 15% discount baseline.
- Monthly true-ups to minimize stranded capacity.

Option B — 24-month firm
- 12-month price floor; 24-month firm with 22% discount.
- Price-sensitivity trigger: if GPU index rises >18% vs baseline for two consecutive quarters, Redwood may (a) invoke a capped renegotiation, or (b) convert a portion of committed units into billable overage with credit.

Marcus — I added a sensitivity tab with P50/P90 and a "worst-case +25%" GPU cost column as requested; highlights on rows 12–15 show margin deltas. Quick ask: can Finance confirm whether the credit cap (we modeled at 8% of total contract value) is acceptable? If yes, I think we can show both options to Helio next week and fast-follow with legal redlines.

Sarah — would you prefer a short sync on Friday 11/13 at 10:00 PT to align on final language? I can include legal if helpful.

Thanks,
Olga
Principal, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
